memory_versions.text:
Order intake lessons:
- Form version 1 requires exactly these fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Source aliases must be normalized: customer -> cust; quantity -> qty.
- “Ordinary priority” or other front-desk notes do not substitute for an explicit priority field/value.
- Always include both priority and ship_country. Omitting either causes rejection; records can fail repeatedly if fields are added one at a time.
- Before submitting, validate that all six required fields are present and correctly named, including qty (not quantity), priority, and ship_country.
- A complete normalized record was accepted on the second attempt for ORD-5101 and ORD-5103.
- Each record has at most three attempts; if still invalid after attempt 3, it goes to manual review.

Order intake lessons:
- Forms v1, v2, and v3 observed the same six required fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Normalize aliases before submission: customer -> cust; quantity -> qty. Do not submit source names customer or quantity.
- Front-desk comments such as “ordinary priority,” “marked ordinary priority,” or other notes do not provide an explicit priority value. Do not infer priority.
- Always provide explicit values for both priority and ship_country. Missing either causes rejection.
- Validate the complete normalized record before submitting: all six fields must be present, correctly named, and populated, including qty (not quantity), priority, and ship_country.
- Validate all fields at once rather than correcting one field per attempt; repeated partial corrections can exhaust the attempt limit.
- These requirements appear unchanged across form versions 1–3. Treat the listed form fields as authoritative, regardless of version.
- A complete normalized record was accepted on the second attempt for ORD-5101 and ORD-5103.
- Recent incomplete records (ORD-5110–ORD-5119) repeatedly failed for missing priority/ship_country and, in some cases, qty; several exhausted all three attempts and went to manual review.
- Each record has at most three attempts. If validation still fails after attempt 3, stop and expect manual review.

Order intake lessons:
- Forms v1–v3 require exactly six fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Form v4 changes the date field: use date, not order_date. Do not submit both; version-specific field lists are authoritative.
- Normalize aliases before submission: customer -> cust; quantity -> qty. Do not submit source names customer or quantity.
- Always provide explicit values for priority and ship_country. Front-desk comments such as “ordinary priority,” “marked ordinary priority,” or confirmation-email requests do not supply valid values; never infer priority or country.
- Validate the complete, normalized record against the current form version before submitting. Check names, presence, and populated values all at once, including qty, priority, ship_country, and the correct date field.
- Do not rely on requirements from an earlier version: v4 records rejected date/order_date mismatches even when other values were present.
- Repeated partial corrections can exhaust attempts. Each record has at most three attempts; after attempt 3, stop and expect manual review.
- Complete normalized records were accepted on the second attempt for ORD-5101 and ORD-5103.
- ORD-5110–5119, ORD-5120–5124, and ORD-5125–5129 show repeated failures from missing priority/ship_country, missing qty, or using order_date on v4. ORD-5121, ORD-5124, and ORD-5127 exhausted all attempts and went to manual review.

Order intake lessons:
- Forms v1–v3 require exactly six fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Forms v4 and v5 require exactly: cust, date, email, priority, qty, ship_country. Do not submit order_date for v4/v5 or submit both; the current version’s field list is authoritative.
- Normalize aliases before submission: customer -> cust; quantity -> qty. Never submit source names customer or quantity.
- Require explicit, valid values for priority and ship_country. Front-desk statements such as “ordinary priority,” “marked ordinary priority,” confirmation-email requests, duplicate checks, customer calls, or portal/transcription notes do not provide values; never infer them.
- A numeric-looking priority (for example, 2) is not necessarily valid; validate it against accepted values along with ship_country.
- Validate the complete normalized record in one pass before submitting: exact field names, no extras, all fields populated, correct date field, qty, priority, and ship_country.
- Do not rely on earlier-version requirements. v4 and v5 reject date/order_date mismatches.
- Each record has at most three attempts. Avoid partial corrections; after attempt 3, stop and expect manual review.
- Complete normalized records were accepted on the second attempt for ORD-5101 and ORD-5103.
- ORD-5110–5129 and ORD-5130–5139 demonstrate repeated rejection when priority/ship_country are missing or invalid, qty is missing, or order_date is used for v4/v5. ORD-5121, ORD-5124, ORD-5127, ORD-5130, ORD-5133, and ORD-5136 exhausted attempts and went to manual review.

Order intake lessons:
- Forms v1–v3 require exactly: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Forms v4–v5 require exactly: cust, date, email, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Forms v6–v7 require exactly: cust, date, email, priority, ship_country, units. Use the current form’s field list; never submit order_date for v4+ or both date fields.
- Normalize aliases by version: customer -> cust; quantity -> qty for v1–v5; quantity -> units for v6–v7. Never submit source names customer or quantity.
- Validate the complete normalized record in one pass: exact field names, no extras, all fields populated, correct date field, and valid qty/units, priority, and ship_country.
- Priority and ship_country require explicit accepted values. Do not infer them from “ordinary priority,” “marked ordinary priority,” confirmation-email requests, duplicate checks, customer calls, portal/transcription notes, or similar statements.
- Numeric-looking priorities (including 0, 1, or 2) are not valid unless explicitly validated against accepted values. Recent v6/v7 records confirm these remain invalid.
- Do not submit error/status/order_id/reason objects as order data.
- Each record has at most three attempts. Avoid partial corrections; after attempt 3, stop and expect manual review.
- Complete normalized records were accepted on the second attempt for ORD-5101 and ORD-5103.
- ORD-5110–5149 show repeated rejection for missing/invalid priority or ship_country, missing qty/units, incorrect date fields, or unvalidated numeric priorities. ORD-5121, ORD-5124, ORD-5127, ORD-5130, ORD-5133, ORD-5136, ORD-5142, ORD-5145, and ORD-5148 exhausted attempts and went to manual review.

Order intake lessons:
- Forms v1–v3 require exactly: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Forms v4–v5 require exactly: cust, date, email, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Forms v6–v7 require exactly: cust, date, email, priority, ship_country, units. Use only the current form’s fields; never submit order_date for v4+ or both date fields.
- Normalize aliases by version: customer → cust; quantity → qty for v1–v5; quantity → units for v6–v7. Never submit source names customer or quantity.
- Validate the complete normalized record in one pass: exact fields, no extras, all populated, correct date field, valid date, qty/units, priority, and ship_country.
- Priority and ship_country require explicit accepted values. Never infer them from “ordinary priority,” “marked ordinary priority,” confirmation-email requests, duplicate checks, customer calls, partner portals, handwritten/transcription notes, or similar statements. Recent v7 batches ORD-5150–5159 repeatedly confirm this.
- Numeric-looking priorities, including 0, 1, and 2, are invalid unless explicitly validated against accepted values.
- Do not submit error/status/order_id/reason objects as order data.
- Each record has at most three attempts. Avoid partial corrections; if required values are missing or invalid, do not guess. After attempt 3, stop and expect manual review.
- Complete normalized records were accepted on the second attempt for ORD-5101 and ORD-5103.
- ORD-5110–5159 show repeated rejection for missing/invalid priority or ship_country, missing qty/units, incorrect date fields, or unvalidated numeric priorities. Exhausted/manual-review records include ORD-5121, 5124, 5127, 5130, 5133, 5136, 5142, 5145, 5148, 5151, 5154, and 5157.
